verdict.rationale: Modal markets very high concurrency ('hundreds of thousands of concurrent rollout environments', 'scale to thousands of concurrent runs') and even documents a backend upgrade for higher creation rates/concurrency, plus community reports of building scalable runner fleets on Sandboxes, showing the capability is real and used at scale. However there is no evidence of documented hard limits, quotas, or per-account/per-plan concurrency ceilings that a platform engineer could plan capacity against. Missing for 10: explicit documented concurrency/rate limits or quotas, benchmark/load-test data, and any per-tier scaling caps.
